dr-ashwin-m-shah.bio:
Dr. Ashwin M Shah is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospital, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, and has worked in the field for more than 31 years.

His listed radiation practice covers the conventional and conformal range — external beam radiotherapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy — together with the focused techniques used for smaller, well-defined targets: stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. He also performs intraoperative radiation therapy.

Brachytherapy is a distinct strand of his work, covering both intracavitary and interstitial placement. After MBBS, MD (Radiotherapy) and DNB (Radiotherapy), he completed a Fellowship in Brachytherapy through a collaborative programme involving Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Apollo Hospitals, with training exposure at Tata Memorial Hospital and the Gujarat Cancer Research Institute. He also trained for a year at S.V. Medical College, Tirupati, through RIMS Hospital, and holds the FIRO national fellowship of the Indian Association of Radiation Oncologists.

Before Apollo Health City in Jubilee Hills, Dr. Shah was associated with KIMS Hospital and Yashoda Hospitals in Hyderabad, the Indo-American Cancer Hospital and Research Institute, Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences, Basavatarakam Indo-American Cancer Hospital, and Government General Hospital in Tirupati.

He has authored and co-authored peer-reviewed publications on chemoradiotherapy in oesophageal and cervical cancers, hypofractionated radiation outcomes, and brachytherapy for cervical and endometrial cancers, alongside studies on brain metastases, breast cancer and prostate cancer, radiation technique comparisons across IMRT, 3D conformal radiotherapy and IGRT, and concurrent chemoradiation versus radiation alone in solid tumours. He is a member of ASTRO and of the Indian Association of Radiation Oncologists across all chapters.

dr-dodul-mondal.bio:
Dr. Dodul Mondal is Principal Director of Radiation Oncology at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket, in Delhi NCR, with more than 18 years in the specialty.

The cancers he works with are broad: musculoskeletal tumours, head-and-neck cancer, neuro-oncology, breast cancer, gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary cancers, thoracic cancers and paediatric oncology. His profile also records involvement in surgical oncology across head and neck, breast, gastrointestinal and thoracic sites, which places his radiation planning alongside the surgical side of those programmes.

Technically, his listed expertise includes proton beam therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery, as well as brachytherapy and total body irradiation.

Dr. Mondal completed MBBS with honours and a gold medal, then MD and DNB in Radiation Oncology. He went on to a UICC fellowship in the United States and further US fellowship training in precision radiation oncology and proton beam therapy, which is consistent with the proton work listed on his profile. Before Max Healthcare he was at Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in New Delhi, the National Cancer Institute at AIIMS Delhi, and Dharamshila Narayana Hospital.

He is a member of the Indian College of Radiation Oncology, the National Academy of Medical Sciences, India, ESTRO, ASTRO, the American Brachytherapy Society, the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, and the Indian Society of Oncology. His recognitions include the UICC-ICRETT Fellowship awarded in 2016 by the Union for International Cancer Control, a CSIR travel grant for the 2016 World Cancer Congress in Paris, and travel grants from the St Gallen Cancer Committee and ICMR for the 14th St Gallen Breast Cancer Conference in Vienna in 2015.

dr-sridhar-p-s.bio:
Dr. Sridhar P S is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 28 years in the specialty.

His listed techniques run from the established to the highly focused. Day-to-day work includes external beam radiotherapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy. Where a target is small and sharply defined, his profile records stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, delivered with CyberKnife and Gamma Knife radiosurgery. Brachytherapy forms a separate part of the practice and covers both intracavitary and interstitial placement.

His qualifications are DMRT, a Diploma in Radiation Therapy, DNB training in radiotherapy, and FRCR, Fellow of the Royal College of Radiologists. He is proficient in English, Kannada and Hindi.

Alongside clinical work, Dr. Sridhar has held a substantial amount of professional office. He has served as President of the Association of Radiation Oncology of India, as Joint Secretary of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, as Joint Secretary of the Neuro Oncology Society in Bangalore, and as Secretary of the Indian Association of Hyperthermic Oncology. His memberships include ASTRO, ASCO, AROI, ESMO, and the Indian Academy of Medical Sciences with the National Malhotra Society of Medical Oncology.

His fellowships and awards are recorded across several years: an International and Travelling Fellowship in Radiation Oncologists of India from 2003 to 2007, the Best Association of Radiation Oncologists of India Fellowship for 2007–2008, a Commonwealth Fellowship from 2005 to 2006 covering cancer research from India to the United Kingdom, and a Teaching Scholarship awarded by the Bihar Pradesh chapter of AROI in 2009.

dr-pradeep-kumar-karumanchi.bio:
Dr. Pradeep Kumar Karumanchi is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, Hyderabad, with more than 16 years of experience.

He treats head and neck, brain, breast, lung, prostate, gastrointestinal and gynaecological cancers with radiation, and has additional training in thoracic and uro-oncology. His technical scope is recorded as CyberKnife radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, brachytherapy and total body irradiation. He is also trained in MR-LINAC and adaptive MRI-guided radiotherapy, 4D gated radiation therapy, hypofractionation, and functional radiosurgery for selected benign conditions.

His training is split between India and abroad. He completed MBBS at Osmania Medical College in Hyderabad and DNB in Radiation Oncology at Healthcare Global Cancer Hospital. He then studied precision oncology at the Université de Genève in Switzerland and thoracic oncology at the University of Michigan in the United States, completed CyberKnife CNS and physician training with Accuray in the United States, and has undertaken training at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. He holds ECFMG certification.

Dr. Karumanchi is a member of the American Society of Clinical Oncology, the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and the Bangalore Oncology Group. He sits on the executive committee of the International Association of Oncology, the organising committee of the Asia Pacific Cancer Congress, and the international core group of the student movement of International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War. His recognitions include India's Best Doctor Award for Excellence in Oncology in 2024 and the APJ Abdul Kalam Health Awards the same year. His academic interests include radiomics and artificial intelligence in oncology.

dr-naman-utreja.bio:
Dr. Naman Utreja is Head of Department and Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector 8, Faridabad, in Delhi NCR, with more than 13 years of experience.

His practice covers head and neck, thoracic, breast, gynaecological, musculoskeletal, genitourinary and paediatric cancers, and his profile also lists medical oncology among his specializations. Two further areas are recorded separately: geriatric oncology, and pain, palliative and end-of-life oncology care. His radiotherapy techniques include image-guided radiation therapy, VMAT and RapidArc, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and brachytherapy.

Dr. Utreja completed MBBS at MGM Medical College in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, and MD in Radiation Oncology at the Swami Rama Himalayan Institute in Dehradun. He also holds a fellowship in treating oncology patients during COVID-19 from Scientia in Los Angeles. Before Sarvodaya, he was associated with the GS Cancer Research Institute and Medical College, Fortis Hospital in Noida, Max Hospital at Shalimar Bagh and at Saket, the Asian Institute and Hospital in Faridabad, and Medanta – The Medicity in Gurgaon.

His academic record is documented across several years. He published in AROICON neuro-oncology in 2014, took second prize in the best paper category in neuro-oncology in 2015, presented a poster at NZAROICON in Hisar in 2017, was faculty at the Breast Cancer Contouring Masterclass at Max Hospital PPG in 2018, and gave an oral presentation at the SBRT and SRS Masterclass at Medanta in 2019. He was a co-investigator on the multi-institutional phase III KINDLE lung cancer study in 2020 and a phase III prostate cancer study in 2022. He is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and its North Zone association.

dr-m-janarthinakani.bio:
Dr. M. Janarthinakani is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Rela Hospital in Chennai, with more than 25 years of experience and medical oncology listed alongside radiation oncology among his specializations.

His clinical work covers radiation therapy for cancer, image-guided and intensity-modulated radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and brachytherapy. His profile also records chemotherapy for cancer and cancer immunotherapy, and two disease sites where he handles the radiation management specifically: cervical cancer and hypopharyngeal cancer.

He completed MBBS at Madurai Medical College in Tamil Nadu between 1995 and 2001, then MD in Radiation Oncology at Cancer Institute Adyar (WIA) in Chennai between 2001 and 2004. In February 2004 he undertook hands-on training in newer techniques in molecular oncology sponsored by the Department of Science and Technology in New Delhi. He completed a certified palliative training course at the Lakshmi Palliative Care Centre in 2016 and passed the ESMO examination in Chennai on 8 October of the same year.

His research includes co-investigator roles in a phase III study of chemotherapy plus immunotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer between 2008 and 2010, and a phase III gastric–oesophageal junction study between 2009 and 2012. His dissertation examined the role of hyperthermia in managing locally advanced carcinoma of the uterine cervix, and at the 2005 Tamil Nadu state AROI meeting he presented on surgery followed by postoperative irradiation compared with irradiation alone in hypopharyngeal carcinoma.

Earlier appointments include Cancer Institute (WIA) Adyar, Government Medical College Tuticorin, RGGGH–BIRO in Chennai, Kumaran Hospital under the Madras Cancer Care Foundation, Billroth Hospital and Apollo Hospital Teynampet. He is a member of AROI and ICON.

dr-s-alex-antony-prasad.bio:
Dr. S. Alex Antony Prasad is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at MGM Healthcare in Chennai, with more than 30 years of experience and medical oncology recorded alongside radiation oncology among his specializations.

His clinical focus is brain tumours, head and neck cancers, breast cancers and other solid tumours. The techniques listed on his profile include image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, along with brachytherapy, plaque brachytherapy and total body irradiation.

His training was largely completed at two of the institutions most associated with Indian radiotherapy. After MBBS at Madurai Kamaraj University, he took a DMRT in Medical Radiation Therapy and an MD in Radiotherapy and Clinical Oncology at Tata Memorial Hospital through the University of Bombay, then the DNB in Radiotherapy from the National Board of Examinations in New Delhi. Internationally, he was an International Outreach Fellow at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in the United States and trained at Christie Hospital in the United Kingdom.

Beyond MGM Healthcare and MGM Cancer Institute, he is a visiting consultant at Kauvery Hospital, Kovilambakkam, and Dr. Rai Memorial Hospital. He has served as President of the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry chapter of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and as National Joint Secretary of the Indian Brachytherapy Society. He is a member of the ASTRO International Committee and the UICC International Review Panel, an editorial board member of the South Asian Journal of Cancer, and has been faculty, speaker and panelist at ASCO, ESMO, ESTRO and AROI meetings. He received the Best Doctor Award from The Tamil Nadu Dr. M.G.R. Medical University.

dr-dipali-bhorikar-borade.bio:
Dr. Dipali Bhorikar Borade is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Navi Mumbai, with more than nine years of experience.

Her disease-site focus is gastrointestinal, head-and-neck, breast and gynaecological cancers. The techniques recorded on her profile include intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, external beam radiotherapy and stereotactic body radiation therapy, together with CyberKnife radiosurgery. Brachytherapy forms a separate part of her practice and covers both intracavitary and interstitial placement. Her profile also lists chemotherapy for solid tumours and adjuvant chemotherapy, the drug treatment given after primary treatment to reduce the chance of recurrence.

Dr. Borade holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB in Radiation Oncology, and her listed qualifications extend to advanced certifications and training in ECRT, ARRT, IGRT, VMAT, SRS and SBRT. Her training and previous posts span Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai, Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital in Varanasi, Mahatma Gandhi Cancer Hospital in Vizag, Maharashtra Cancer Centre in Pune, and Apollo Hospital in Navi Mumbai, where she now practises.

Her academic record sits alongside that clinical work. She received oral presentation awards at a Best Paper session of the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology meeting in Barcelona, has presented papers at AROI national conferences and symposia, and has given multiple poster presentations at international cancer conferences including ESMO and ASTRO related forums. Her peer-reviewed publications have covered stereotactic body radiotherapy, chemotherapy combinations, and treatment outcomes across several cancer types.

She is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and of the Indian Medical Council.

dr-anil-kumar-anand.bio:
Dr. Anil Kumar Anand is Principal Director and Head of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Delhi NCR, with more than 33 years of experience.

His practice spans both the external-beam and brachytherapy sides of the specialty. On the external-beam side his profile lists conventional external beam radiotherapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, alongside the focused techniques used for compact targets: stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. He also performs intraoperative radiation therapy, delivered during surgery, and works with intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Head-and-neck oncology is a distinct thread in his background. After MBBS at Dayanand Medical College in Ludhiana and an MD in Radiotherapy and Oncology at the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research in Chandigarh, he completed specialised training in radiation therapy at the New York Hospital Medical Centre of Queens in the United States and specialised training in radiotherapy of head and neck cancers at The Middlesex Hospital Medical School in London.

Before Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Gurgaon, he worked at Max Hospital in Saket, the Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute, Batra Hospital in New Delhi, the Medical Research Center in New Delhi, and PGI Chandigarh.

Dr. Anand is a member of the Indian Society of Oncology, the American Society of Radiation Oncology and the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India. He has served as an advisor to ICRO, the WHO and other UN organisations, and is an editorial board member of the Journal of Cancer Research and Therapeutics.

dr-debnarayan-dutta.bio:
Dr. Debnarayan Dutta is a Senior Consultant Radiation Oncologist and Clinical Director of Radiation Oncology at Yashoda Hospitals, Hi-Tech City, Hyderabad, with more than 19 years of experience. Neuro-oncology and head-and-neck cancer sit at the centre of his practice, with a particular emphasis on radiosurgery.

His technical work covers CyberKnife radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and brachytherapy. He currently oversees the CyberKnife facility at Yashoda Hospitals and previously managed a radiosurgery programme at Amrita Hospital in Kochi, and he is credited as a pioneer in introducing the CyberKnife radiosurgery facility in India in 2010.

Dr. Dutta completed his MBBS before an MD in Radiation Oncology at Calcutta University, Kolkata, between 2003 and 2006. He went on to a fellowship in Neuro-Oncology from 2006 to 2008 and a fellowship in Head & Neck IMRT from 2008 to 2010. His PhD, awarded by VIT, Vellore, in 2023, examined molecular profiling in Indian patients with head-and-neck cancer treated with radical-intent image-guided radiotherapy. Earlier appointments took him to Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai, Apollo Cancer Hospital in Chennai and Amrita Hospital in Kochi.

He has published more than 150 indexed papers, contributed three book chapters and authored four books, and has been an invited speaker at over 250 national and international meetings. He belongs to the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the Indian Society of Neurooncology and the Medical Council of India. His honours include an ASCO Merit Award at Chicago in 2008, the Nucletron Fellowship Award at AROICON 2010 and the ISNO Presidential Award for Best Clinical Researcher in 2024.

dr-bharath-chandra-gurram.bio:
Dr. Bharath Chandra Gurram is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, Hyderabad, with more than 13 years of experience. He works across radiation oncology and medical oncology, and his clinical interests cover head and neck, thoracic, gastrointestinal and genitourinary cancers, together with palliative care and cancer nutrition.

His radiation practice includes stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, brachytherapy and total body irradiation, allowing treatment to be matched to the site and stage of disease.

Dr. Gurram completed his MBBS at Dr. NTR University of Health Sciences between 2005 and 2010, followed by an internship at Chalmeda Anand Rao Institute of Medical Sciences. He then took his MD in Radiation Oncology at Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences, Kochi, from 2012 to 2015. His subsequent credentials include MRCP through the SCE in Medical Oncology in the UK in 2019 and FESMO certification from the European Society of Medical Oncology in 2014. He has also completed the Certification Course in Essentials of Palliative Care, an Indian College of Radiation Oncology teaching course, Basic Life Support with the American Heart Association, and EMPACT emergency and procedural training at Apollo Hospital.

He practises across Yashoda Hospitals at Somajiguda and Hitec City, and is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the American Brachytherapy Society, the American Society for Radiation Oncology and the European Society of Medical Oncology. His awards include the AROI Neil Joseph Fellowship Award at Imphal in 2014, a travel grant for a paper selected among the top five at the same conference, a gold medal at the SACR 2013 quiz and a silver medal for a poster presentation at Adyar, Chennai.

dr-garima-singh.bio:
Dr. Garima Singh is Principal Consultant in Radiation Oncology at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 14 years of experience. Her practice spans head and neck, breast, lung and thoracic, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, thyroid and gynaecological cancers, as well as bone and soft-tissue sarcoma, lymphoma and paediatric cancer programmes.

Across these disease groups she uses 3D conformal and external beam radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. Her brachytherapy work covers both intracavitary and interstitial techniques, and she also performs intraoperative radiation therapy.

Dr. Singh holds an MBBS and an MD. She completed a fellowship in recent advances in radiation oncology at Dharmshila Cancer Hospital & Research Centre in New Delhi and an observership at the Community Cancer Center in Indianapolis, which is affiliated with M.D. Anderson. Her earlier appointments trace a path through several of the region's teaching and tertiary institutions: consultant at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket, associate consultant at Medanta – The Medicity in Gurgaon, senior research associate at Maulana Azad Medical College, assistant professor at Safdarjung Hospital and senior resident at Maulana Azad Medical College and L.N.J.P Hospital.

She is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the Indian Brachytherapy Society and the Indian Society of Clinical Oncology. For patients travelling for treatment, her profile combines a broad organ-site practice with the full range of external beam, stereotactic and brachytherapy techniques available at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital.

dr-shyam-singh-bisht.bio:
Dr. Shyam Singh Bisht is Director of Radiation Oncology at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 18 years of experience. Lung, breast and prostate cancers form the core of his clinical interests, alongside cranial radiosurgery.

His technical practice is built around high-precision delivery. He works with stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, and he also performs external beam radiotherapy together with intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Dr. Bisht completed his MBBS and an MD in Radiation Oncology, and was a postgraduate at KGMU, Lucknow. He added a Post Graduate Diploma in Clinical Research, and his advanced training includes a fellowship in Functional & Stereotactic Radiosurgery in France, a fellowship in high-precision radiation covering SRS and SBRT, and dedicated CyberKnife radiosurgery training in cranial and extracranial radiosurgery. That sequence of training maps closely onto the stereotactic work he leads at Medanta.

Alongside clinical practice he has authored more than 50 full-text international publications and contributed to four oncology textbooks. His recognitions include the G.C. Pant Young Doctor Award at a national conference in 2010, the ESTRO Varian Award in Spain in 2015, an ESMO travel grant in Singapore in 2016 and an AROI Overseas Fellowship in 2022, and he has been a gold medallist three times at national conferences. Patients considering high-precision radiation treatment will find a practice concentrated on stereotactic and image-guided techniques and supported by sustained academic work in the same field.

dr-p-vijay-anand-reddy.bio:
Dr. P. Vijay Anand Reddy is Director of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospital, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, with more than 30 years of experience. His clinical and research interests centre on head and neck cancers, gynecological cancers, brain tumors and brain metastases, and localized prostate cancer.

His technical expertise covers intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. He also works with 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy, intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, and intraoperative radiation therapy, which together allow treatment to be tailored from routine curative-intent courses to highly focused single-site work.

Dr. Reddy holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology, a DNB in Radiotherapy and a fellowship in Radiation Oncology, and practises at Apollo Cancer Centre, Jubilee Hills. His research portfolio spans stereotactic radiosurgery, IMRT, brachytherapy and treatment outcomes in head and neck cancers, gynecological cancers, brain tumors and other malignancies, and has been presented at ASTRO, ESTRO and national conferences. A prospective study of neurocognitive function, performance status, quality of life and local control in patients with one to three newly diagnosed brain metastases treated with stereotactic radiosurgery alone received the Best Scientific Paper Award at AROICON 2015, and a feasibility study of hypofractionated radiotherapy for clinically localized carcinoma of the prostate received the same award at AROICON 2014.

He is President of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and a member of ASCO, ASTRO, ESMO and the Union for International Cancer Control. In 2017 he was recognised as "The Legend in the Field of Oncology" at the Times Healthcare Achievers Awards in Hyderabad.

dr-azmi-saundarya-k.bio:
Dr. Azmi Saundarya K is Clinical Lead and Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Gleneagles HealthCity Chennai, with more than 8 years of experience. She treats breast, gynaecological, head and neck, thoracic, gastrointestinal, central nervous system and skin cancers, along with soft-tissue sarcomas and selected benign conditions such as keloids.

Her radiotherapy work includes image-guided and intensity-modulated techniques, stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, brachytherapy and total body irradiation, giving her a range of options for both curative and supportive treatment.

Dr. Azmi holds an MBBS, a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy from Amrita Institute of Medical Sciences and a DNB in Radiation Oncology completed at Apollo Specialty Hospital, Chennai. She received ECFMG certification in 2014 and completed the Global Fellowship in Palliative Medicine with Pallium India in the 2024 batch. Her continuing education includes the International Workshop on Precision Radiotherapy in Trivandrum in 2015, the ESTRO School and AROI course on advanced technologies in New Delhi in December 2015, the Christie-TMC FRCR course at Tata Medical Centre, Kolkata, in January 2017, and an observership in advanced brachytherapy and image-guided IMRT at Long Beach Memorial Medical Center in California.

She is affiliated with Gleneagles Hospital at Perumbakkam, Rela Hospitals, MIOT International and Jus Onco at Kodambakkam, all in Chennai, and has been a member of the Tamilnadu Medical Council and the Indian Medical Council since November 2009 as well as the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India. Her combined training in radiation oncology and palliative medicine supports both disease-directed radiotherapy and symptom-focused care.

dr-vijay-bhasker-l.bio:
Dr. Vijay Bhasker L is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 20 years of experience. Head and neck cancer is a recurring focus of his clinical and academic work, particularly the experience of patients during a course of radiation treatment.

His radiation expertise includes intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery. He performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, and his practice also covers chemotherapy for solid tumors in the adjuvant and neoadjuvant settings.

Dr. Bhasker holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB in Radiation Oncology from the National Board. He practises at Apollo Hospitals on Bannerghatta Road and consults in English, Hindi and Kannada, which is a practical consideration for families arranging treatment in Bangalore.

His research has concentrated on how radiation treatment affects patients' daily lives. He received the Best Case Reports 2011 award, presented at Kidwai Memorial Institute of Oncology in Bangalore, for an assessment of health-related quality of life in head and neck cancer patients receiving radiation therapy. He has presented related work on the effects of different radiation doses on patient-reported quality of life outcomes at the J.N. Tata Auditorium at IISc, and has taken findings on radiation-related adverse effects to national and international oncology forums. His published work includes a contribution to Advances in Molecular Imaging & Radiation Oncology/Genomics, and he was recognised at the IISc World Cancer Congress for his contribution to radiation oncology research.

dr-aditi-aggarwal-1.bio:
Dr. Aditi Aggarwal is a Radiation Oncologist at Apollo Athenaa Women's Cancer Centre, Delhi NCR, with more than 18 years of experience. Gastrointestinal radiation oncology is a defined area of her practice, alongside general radiation oncology.

She delivers radiation therapy for cancer using image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and brachytherapy, and she also consults at Apollo Hospitals in Delhi.

Dr. Aggarwal holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a PDCR. Her academic record began with a gold medal in pharmacology and a university gold medal in gynecology and obstetrics, and in 2012 she received the Young Investigator Award from the British Journal of Radiology.

Her research reflects both the technical and the organisational sides of cancer care. She contributed to an ESTRO poster in 2016 on adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer, describing a hybrid approach that combines online image guidance with offline adaptation. In the Journal of Global Oncology in 2017 she co-authored a paper on the organization of chemotherapy and systemic therapy services in India, and in the same year she co-authored a Journal of Clinical Oncology abstract on discordance in the histopathological diagnosis of patients with soft tissue sarcoma referred to a tertiary care centre.

She is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and its Maharashtra State Chapter, the Indian Brachytherapy Society, the Gastrointestinal Oncology Society and the Society of Genitourinary Oncologists. Together these strands give patients a radiation oncologist whose gastrointestinal focus is matched by experience with adaptive, image-guided, stereotactic and brachytherapy techniques.

dr-khushboo-rastogi.bio:
Dr. Khushboo Rastogi is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 5 years of experience. She treats thoracic and lung, head and neck, breast, thyroid, gastrointestinal, gynaecological and urological cancers with radiation, as well as sarcomas, bone cancers and lymphomas.

Her technical practice covers 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. She also works with CyberKnife radiosurgery, intraoperative radiation therapy, and intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, so treatment can be planned around the site, size and position of the tumour.

Dr. Rastogi holds an MBBS and an MD in Radiation Oncology, and completed the Certification Course in Essentials of Palliative Care run by the IAPC in Gujarat. Her professional path before BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital included radiation oncology positions at Sterling Hospitals in Gujarat and Manipal Hospitals in Delhi, a research fellowship at Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai and senior residency at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket.

Her memberships include the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the Indian Brachytherapy Society, the Gastrointestinal Oncology Society and the International Organisation for Radiotherapy for Benign Conditions, the last of which reflects the benign-disease side of her radiotherapy work. For patients and families, this background brings together organ-specific radiation oncology, high-precision external beam techniques, brachytherapy and formal training in palliative care.

dr-prahlad-yathiraj.bio:
Dr. Prahlad Yathiraj is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at MGM Healthcare, Chennai, with more than 15 years of experience. His practice brings together routine radiation therapy for cancer and the more focused techniques used when a tumour has to be treated to a high dose in a small number of sessions.

He works with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, image-guided radiation therapy, brachytherapy and plaque brachytherapy, intraoperative radiation therapy and total body irradiation. The mix covers everything from single-site stereotactic treatment to the whole-body conditioning used before transplant.

His training has been built across India, Canada and the United States. He gained clinical training and experience at Kasturba Medical College and at Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai, completed advanced training in liver and spine SBRT at Princess Margaret Hospital in Toronto, and held a UICC Fellowship in head and neck cancer at the University of Michigan. That combination explains the two strands running through his practice: stereotactic treatment of abdominal and spinal disease, and head and neck oncology.

Alongside patient care, Dr. Yathiraj has more than 17 peer-reviewed publications in oncology journals and has presented at ASTRO, ESTRO and ASCO. He serves as Treasurer of the AROI Tamil Nadu and Puducherry chapter of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, and outside medicine he has represented alumni cricket teams internationally.

dr-anusheel-munshi.bio:
Dr. Anusheel Munshi is Principal Director and Head of Radiation Oncology at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 28 years of experience. He practises specifically as a radiation oncologist while contributing to collaborative surgical and medical oncology programmes, and his clinical work spans head-and-neck, thoracic and lung, breast, thyroid, gastrointestinal, gynaecological, urological and paediatric cancers as well as bone and soft-tissue sarcoma.

His technical range covers 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. He also delivers conventional external beam treatment, intraoperative radiation therapy, and intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, so the technique can follow the tumour rather than the other way round.

Dr. Munshi holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB in Radiation Oncology, and is a gold medallist. His international training includes the Novartis AROI Overseas Fellowship at The Royal Marsden Hospital in the United Kingdom and a UICC ICRETT Fellowship at Long Beach Memorial Hospital in California.

Before his current role he worked at Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai, at Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Gurgaon, at Manipal Hospital in Dwarka and at the International Oncology Cancer Institute at Fortis Hospital, Noida. That mix of tertiary cancer centre and multi-speciality hospital experience sits behind the multidisciplinary cancer programmes he now takes part in at BLK-Max Super Speciality Hospital in New Delhi.

dr-srinivas-chilukuri.bio:
Dr. Srinivas Chilukuri is a Senior Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Apollo Proton Cancer Centre, Chennai, with more than 22 years of experience in radiation oncology.

Proton beam therapy is a central part of his practice. Alongside it he works with intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy, which together cover the main approaches to delivering radiation from outside the body. His stereotactic work includes stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery, and he also performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, where the radiation source is placed in or beside the tumour. For a patient weighing up treatment options, that breadth means the choice of technique can be made on clinical grounds.

Dr. Chilukuri holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a PDCR qualification, and he topped the Mumbai University MD Radiation Oncology examination. In September 2006 he stood first at the Indian College of Radiation Oncology annual teaching course and received its Young Achiever Award, and in the same year he won the national oncology quiz at AROICON 2006.

His professional memberships connect him to several international oncology communities: the American Society of Clinical Oncology, the American Society for Radiation Oncology, the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology and the European Society for Medical Oncology. His background brings together proton therapy, advanced photon techniques and brachytherapy within a single centre.

dr-sandeep-de.bio:
Dr. Sandeep De is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Navi Mumbai, with more than 25 years of experience. His clinical work covers brain tumors, lung cancer, head and neck cancers, gastrointestinal malignancies and gynecological cancers.

Across those disease groups he plans treatment using intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. He also performs stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery for tumours that need a high dose delivered to a tightly defined target, and his brachytherapy practice covers both intracavitary and interstitial approaches.

Dr. De earned his MBBS and completed an MD in Radiotherapy at King George's Medical College, Lucknow. He also holds a DNB in Radiotherapy from the National Board of Examinations and the FRCR. His postgraduate clinical background includes senior residency at Tata Memorial Centre & Hospital in Parel, Mumbai, from 2007 to 2010, and a clinical fellowship associated with Fr. Muller Medical College Hospital from 2014 to 2017.

He is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology, the Indian Society of Radiation Oncologists & Oncologic Physicists and the Canadian Association for Radiation Oncology. Patients seen at Apollo Hospitals in CBD Belapur therefore meet a radiation oncologist whose training spans Indian tertiary cancer centres and the UK examination system, with a practice built on the full external beam, stereotactic and brachytherapy toolkit.

dr-kalyani-premchandra.bio:
Dr. Kalyani Premchandra is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 13 years of experience.

Her radiotherapy practice spans external beam treatment, 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery, and she performs both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy. Her work also extends to systemic treatment, including chemotherapy and immunotherapy for solid tumors, palliative chemotherapy and hormone therapy for breast cancer, which is relevant for patients whose plan combines radiation with drug treatment.

Dr. Premchandra holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB in Medical Oncology, and that dual training is reflected in her research. Her MD dissertation assessed the role of intraluminal brachytherapy with concurrent chemoradiotherapy in carcinoma of the esophagus, while her DNB thesis examined treatment-related adverse events of immunotherapy in patients with advanced cancers.

At AROICON 2019 in Thiruvananthapuram she presented a poster on the role of various fractionation schedules of radiation therapy in the treatment of bone metastases. In the same year she received a best paper award at FAMS for a comparison of external beam treatment and brachytherapy in patients with early-stage breast cancer treated with accelerated partial breast irradiation, and she is recognised as an accomplished researcher in radiation oncology. Her practice brings together site-specific radiation techniques, symptom-directed treatment, brachytherapy and the study of treatment toxicity.

dr-k-r-prasanna-kumar.bio:
Dr. K. R. Prasanna Kumar is Senior Consultant and Visiting Radiation Oncologist at Rela Hospital, Chennai, with more than 18 years of experience in radiation oncology.

He treats cancer with a wide span of external beam and brachytherapy techniques. These include intensity-modulated and image-guided radiotherapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and Gamma Knife radiosurgery. His technical background also covers 2D conventional radiotherapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, RapidArc, SRT and X-Knife SRS, and in brachytherapy he works with intracavitary, intraluminal and interstitial high-dose-rate approaches. That range allows planning to move between conventional, highly conformal, stereotactic and internally delivered radiation according to the clinical indication rather than the equipment available.

Dr. Prasanna Kumar earned his MBBS at Madurai Medical College under Tamil Nadu Dr. MGR University between 2002 and 2008, and completed DND Radiotherapy training at Apollo Speciality Hospital, Chennai, from 2009 to 2012. His professional experience includes appointments at Apollo Speciality Hospital, HCG Cancer Centre, SIMS Hospital, Kauvery Hospital and Kamakshi Hospital, all in Chennai, alongside his work at the Rela Hospital cancer centre.

His thesis analysed acute toxicities, pathological complete response and sphincter preservation rate after pre-operative chemoradiation in locally advanced rectal cancers, and he presented a paper on the role of CyberKnife radiosurgery in choroidal melanoma at TN-PY AROI 2012. He is a lifetime member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and a member of the Medical Council of India and the Tamil Nadu Medical Council.

dr-ranjeet-bajpai.bio:
Dr. Ranjeet Bajpai is a Radiation Specialist Oncologist at Apollo Hospitals, Navi Mumbai, with more than 20 years of experience. His practice covers radiation therapy for cancer, brachytherapy and focused stereotactic treatment, including stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery.

Head and neck cancer runs through his academic work, and the questions he has studied are practical ones about how treatment is actually delivered and tolerated. His papers have addressed the quality of recording of patient demography, compliance to radiotherapy, morbidity reporting and follow-up status in head and neck cancer patients; the role of percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy for enteral nutrition in patients on intensive chemo-radiation protocols; and the use of VFG in assessing functional abnormalities after chemo-radiotherapy.

Dr. Bajpai holds an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB, and is licensed with the Medical Council of India and the Maharashtra Medical Council. Between March and October 2022 he completed fellowship training at Sjaelland University Hospital in Copenhagen, Denmark. His professional background also includes Sir HN Reliance Foundation Hospital and PD Hinduja Hospital and Medical Research Centre in Mumbai, and Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow.

He has been a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India since 2004 and joined the European Society for Radiotherapy & Oncology and the American Society for Radiation Oncology in 2008. Two of his conference papers received best paper awards, in 2005 and 2008, and an AROI travel fellowship in 2005 supported his work on nutrition during chemoradiation.

dr-vineeta-goel.bio:
Dr. Vineeta Goel is Senior Director and Head of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Fortis Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi NCR, with more than 26 years of experience.

Her practice covers intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and 3D conformal radiotherapy, along with stereotactic radiosurgery and conventional external beam radiotherapy. She also performs intraoperative radiation therapy and both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, which together allow radiation to be delivered externally, during surgery, or from a source placed within the body.

Dr. Goel earned her MBBS from MGIMS Sewagram, Wardha, in 1997. She then completed a DMRT in Radiation Oncology at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, in 2000 and a DNB in Radiation Oncology at the same institution in 2001, and she received MNAMS in 2019. Her earlier appointments include Tata Memorial Hospital and Max Super Speciality Hospital.

A distinctive feature of her background is the amount of her advanced training taken abroad, each programme matched to a specific technique she uses. She trained in stereotactic body radiation therapy at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in the United States and again at Champalimaud Cancer Centre in Portugal, in intraoperative radiation therapy at Heidelberg in Germany, and in IMRT and IGRT at the Oncology Institute of Southern Switzerland. For patients weighing up a high-precision treatment plan, that training sits directly behind the conformal, image-guided, stereotactic, intraoperative and brachytherapy work she leads at Shalimar Bagh.

dr-indu-bansal-aggarwal.bio:
Dr. Indu Bansal Aggarwal is Group Director and Head of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, Delhi NCR, with more than 27 years of experience. Her clinical interests include radiation treatment for paediatric tumours, head and neck cancers, and cancers affecting adolescents and young adults.

She uses a broad range of external beam approaches, including 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, as well as stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. Her procedural expertise also takes in CyberKnife radiosurgery, intraoperative radiation therapy delivered during an operation, and intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy. Working across younger patients in particular, that span matters: it allows the technique to be selected around the tumour site and the long-term consequences of treatment.

Dr. Aggarwal completed both her MBBS and her MD in Radiation Oncology at Pt. BDS PGIMS, Rohtak. She later earned a Diploma in Hospital Management from the National Institute of Health and Family Welfare in New Delhi, which complements her departmental leadership role. Her advanced training includes an Association of Radiation Oncologists of India fellowship at MD Anderson Cancer Centre in Houston and the association's Neil Joseph Fellowship, and she is described as proficient in advanced radiation procedures.

Her recognitions include being named a Pink Ambassador by the Global Entrepreneurs Clique, a Golden Citizen of India, and a recipient of the National Mahila Gold Rattan Award. At Paras Health in Gurugram she combines clinical radiation oncology with group-level responsibility for the department.

dr-mayur-mayank.bio:
Dr. Mayur Mayank is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 13 years of experience.

His radiation practice includes intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, VMAT, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. He also performs stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy for tightly targeted treatment, along with intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Dr. Mayank holds an MBBS, a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy, an MD in Radiation Oncology and a DNB in Radiotherapy. He undertook oncology training at Christian Medical College, Vellore, and later held a Union for International Cancer Control fellowship with training at Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre in Australia. Before joining Medanta in Gurugram he worked at Metro Cancer Hospital in Faridabad, where he established and started the Department of Radiation Oncology — a useful indication of the planning and set-up experience he brings alongside clinical work.

His academic record includes distinctions in physiology, forensic medicine and ophthalmology during his MBBS training, the AROI award for best oral presentation at AROITNPYCON-2012 at JIPMER, Puducherry, and a Tamil Nadu Dr. MGR Medical University gold medal in 2013 for securing the highest mark in the DMRT. Taken together, his training and appointments have kept him working across high-precision external beam radiation, stereotactic treatment and brachytherapy since the start of his career.

dr-charu-garg.bio:
Dr. Charu Garg is Vice Chairman of Radiation Oncology at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket, Delhi NCR, with more than 25 years of experience. Breast and gynaecological cancers are the focus of her clinical work.

In treating them she applies intensity-modulated and image-guided radiotherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and brachytherapy. Her practice also covers the wider use of radiation therapy for cancer across the disease sites managed within the department, which allows treatment to be shaped around the individual tumour and the patient's overall plan of care.

Dr. Garg earned her MBBS at BJ Medical College, Ahmedabad, and completed her MD in Radiation Oncology at the Gujarat Cancer & Research Institute, also in Ahmedabad. She subsequently took advanced training in radiation techniques at Mannheim, Germany. Her career has included affiliations with Max Healthcare, Rajiv Gandhi Cancer and Research Institute and Medanta – The Medicity, giving her experience across several multidisciplinary cancer centres in the region.

Her professional memberships connect her with both Indian and international oncology organisations: the American Society for Therapeutic Oncology, the Indian Society of Oncology, the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and the Oncology Forum. For patients travelling to Delhi NCR for breast or gynaecological cancer treatment, her profile combines a quarter-century of radiation oncology practice, a defined organ-site focus, and training in conformal, image-guided, stereotactic and brachytherapy techniques.

dr-subodh-chandra-pande.bio:
Dr. Subodh Chandra Pande is Chief of Radiation Oncology and Co-Chief of the CyberKnife Centre at Artemis Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 40 years of experience. Radiation treatment in paediatric oncology and neuro-oncology has been the defining thread of that career.

His radiation expertise covers CyberKnife radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery, image-guided radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy. He consults in English, Hindi and Marathi.

Dr. Pande holds an MD in Radiotherapy from AIIMS, New Delhi, completed in 1997, as well as a DMRE. His earlier appointments include Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai, Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in New Delhi and Bhagwan Mahaveer Cancer Hospital and Research Centre in Jaipur. At Tata Memorial Hospital he helped develop neuro-oncology and paediatric oncology services, and at Indraprastha Apollo he worked on advancing stereotactic radiosurgery facilities — the same two strands he now leads at Artemis Hospital in Gurugram.

Between 1997 and 2000 he served as Secretary General of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India. His other professional bodies reflect the range of his interests: the Indian Society of Oncology, the Association of Medical Physicists of India, the Paediatric Haematology & Oncology Chapter of the Indian Academy of Paediatrics, the International Society of Paediatric Oncology and the Endocrine Society based in New Jersey. For families seeking paediatric or neurological cancer care, his profile combines four decades of clinical practice with sustained involvement in the professional organisations that shape it.

dr-swarupa-mitra.bio:
Dr. Swarupa Mitra is Senior Director and Head of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Delhi NCR, with more than 25 years of experience.

Her clinical expertise spans 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. She also works with external beam radiotherapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, intraoperative radiation therapy delivered during surgery, and both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, so that treatment can be planned around the tumour site rather than a single available technique.

Dr. Mitra holds an MBBS and an MD in Radiation Oncology, and practises at Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Gurgaon.

Alongside her departmental leadership she carries a substantial teaching and mentoring load. She has been invited faculty at the American Society of Clinical Oncology and at the Indian College of Radiation Oncologists, has served as a mentor for the Union for International Cancer Control, and has acted as co-guide for a PhD thesis at the University of Ghent in Belgium.

Her work also extends into public health policy and awareness. She was nominated to the Project Advisory Committee for Health Communication under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, and received a certificate of recognition from the Health Minister of Jharkhand for her contribution to cervical cancer awareness among women in the state. These roles sit alongside a long clinical practice across conformal, image-guided, stereotactic and brachytherapy techniques.

dr-v-balasundaram.bio:
Dr. V. Balasundaram is Head of Department and Clinical Lead for Radiation Oncology at Rela Hospital, Chennai, with more than 30 years of experience.

His practice covers radiation therapy for cancer, brachytherapy, image-guided radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. He also works with concurrent chemoradiation protocols, cancer immunotherapy and targeted therapy, which matters when radiation forms one part of a combined treatment plan.

Dr. Balasundaram earned his MBBS from Thanjavur Medical College between 1987 and 1992, then completed an MD in Radiation Therapy at Madras Medical College & Government General Hospitals, Chennai, from 1996 to 1999. He was Department Head and full-time consultant in radiation oncology at V.S. Hospital, Chetpet, from October 2005 to April 2025, worked as a specialist in clinical oncology at Hospital University Kebangsaan Malaysia in Kuala Lumpur, and was a senior resident in radiotherapy at JIPMER, Puducherry. He now leads radiation oncology at Dr. Rela Institute & Medical Centre in Chrompet.

His research reflects the same clinical interests. He published on external beam radiotherapy and intraluminal brachytherapy in advanced inoperable esophageal cancer in the American Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2001, co-authored a 2010 report on recurrent multiple myeloma presenting as a breast plasmacytoma, and contributed to an ESMO 2013 poster on chemotherapy with concurrent radiation in locally advanced head and neck cancers. In 2016 he wrote a Tamil-language cancer awareness book with Kumudham Magazine, extending his work into public education.

dr-anbarasi-kumaresan.bio:
Dr. Anbarasi Kumaresan is a Senior Consultant Radiation Oncologist at MGM Healthcare, Chennai, with more than 17 years of experience. Her clinical work includes radiotherapy for head and neck cancers, breast cancer and other solid tumours, and she contributes to multidisciplinary cancer care alongside medical oncology colleagues.

She uses intensity-modulated and image-guided radiotherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery and brachytherapy. Her palliative care training sits close to this work: it is directly relevant when symptom relief, rather than cure, is the goal of a course of radiation.

Dr. Kumaresan earned her MBBS from Thoothukudi Government Medical College between 2003 and 2009. She then completed a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy at the Cancer Institute (WIA), Adyar, Chennai, from 2011 to 2013, and stayed on at the same institution for her MDRT from 2013 to 2015. In 2018 she took the Indian Association of Palliative Care certificate course in essentials of palliative care, followed in 2019 by hands-on palliative care training with the IAPC and Lakshmi Pain and Palliative Care.

She is affiliated with MGM Healthcare and MGM Cancer Institute in Chennai. Her professional memberships span Indian and international radiation oncology communities: she is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and a member of the Indian Society of Oncology, the Indian Brachytherapy Society and the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology.

dr-s-jayalakshmi.bio:
Dr. S Jayalakshmi is Head of Radiation Oncology and the CyberKnife Centre (Unit II) at Artemis Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 34 years of experience. Head and neck oncology and gynaecological oncology are her principal clinical interests.

She works across a broad range of radiation techniques, including stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and 3D conformal radiotherapy. Her expertise also covers external beam radiotherapy and both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, the latter being particularly relevant to the gynaecological side of her practice.

Dr. Jayalakshmi earned her MBBS from Stanley Medical College, Chennai, and her MD in Radiation Oncology from Christian Medical College, Vellore, and subsequently completed the DNB in Radiation Oncology. Her advanced training then followed the technology closely: a fellowship in 3DCRT and IMRT at the University of Bristol in the UK, a fellowship in IGRT, SRS and SRT at Yashoda Hospitals in Hyderabad, and a fellowship in CyberKnife SRS, SRT and SBRT with Accuray International in San Jose, California.

That progression, from postgraduate oncology education through conformal and image-guided training to dedicated CyberKnife qualification, is what sits behind her current leadership of the radiation oncology and CyberKnife unit at Artemis Hospitals in Gurugram. She is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India.

dr-y-nalini.bio:
Dr. Y. Nalini is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, Hyderabad, with more than 32 years of experience. Her clinical interests include gastrointestinal, breast, head and neck and gynaecological cancers, as well as brain tumours and paediatric cancers.

Her radiation expertise encompasses image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and brachytherapy.

Dr. Nalini completed her MBBS at Gandhi Medical College, Osmania University, Hyderabad, in 1983. She earned an MD in Radiotherapy at Osmania Medical College and a DNB in Radiotherapy from the National Board of Examinations, both in 1994. Her international training has been technique-specific: a UICC ICRETT fellowship at The Royal Marsden Hospital in London in 2000 on quality assurance in HDR brachytherapy, and advanced IGRT and IMRT training at MD Anderson Cancer Hospital in Houston in 2007.

A notable feature of her profile is the extent of her clinical trial work. She was a co-investigator in the international ATLAS breast cancer treatment trial comparing longer and shorter adjuvant tamoxifen, and in a multicentric study of Wobe Mugose E for reducing radiation toxicity. She was an investigator in the ToGA study of trastuzumab with chemotherapy in HER2-positive advanced gastric cancer, and in a Phase II Asia and Australia study of cetuximab with irinotecan in metastatic colorectal adenocarcinoma expressing EGFR. She is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, ASTRO, the Indian Medical Association and UICC.

dr-m-suneetha.bio:
Dr. M. Suneetha is Senior Consultant Radiation Oncologist and Clinical Director at Yashoda Hospitals, Hi-Tech City, Hyderabad, with more than 25 years of experience. Her clinical interests include gynecological, breast, head and neck, gastrointestinal and neuro-oncological malignancies, with gynecological radiation oncology a particular focus.

Her radiation expertise covers image-guided radiation therapy, brachytherapy, intraoperative radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. Within brachytherapy she has a special interest in MR-guided interstitial hybrid and template techniques, which are used where a tumour needs the radiation source placed directly within it under imaging guidance.

Dr. Suneetha completed her MBBS at Osmania Medical College, Hyderabad, in 1992 and her MD in Radiation Oncology at MNJIORCC, Hyderabad, in 2001. She obtained a DNB from the National Board of Examinations in New Delhi in 2004, and in 2017 completed the FRCR in Clinical Oncology with the Royal College of Radiologists in London.

Her earlier institutional experience includes Continental Hospital and Basavatarakam Indo American Cancer Hospital & Research Institute in Hyderabad, and she also works with the International Oncology Institute at Yashoda Hospitals, Hitec City. She is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, has published in peer-reviewed journals and has presented at national and international conferences and workshops. Her recognitions include the Indira Priyadarshini Young Doctor Award.

dr-tejinder-kataria.bio:
Dr. Tejinder Kataria is Chairperson of Radiation Oncology at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 37 years of experience.

Her radiation expertise includes intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. She also works with stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery, together with intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, giving the department the full range of conformal, focused and internally delivered treatment options.

Dr. Kataria holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiotherapy and a DNB in Radiotherapy. Her advanced training was taken at PGI Chandigarh, the University of Cambridge, the University of Leeds and Harvard University, and she now leads the radiation oncology department at Medanta in Gurugram.

Her distinctions run through every stage of her education and career. She received a National Education Scholarship in 1977, a Himachal State Scholarship for MBBS in 1978 and a DGHS Scholarship for MD Radiotherapy in 1985, and in 2010 she was included in Marquis Who's Who in the World.

For patients travelling to Delhi NCR, the practical point is the combination on offer: a departmental chairperson with nearly four decades in radiation oncology, formal radiotherapy qualifications from India and advanced training at several teaching centres abroad, working across conformal and image-guided external beam radiation, stereotactic treatment and brachytherapy within a single unit.

dr-d-shiva-prasad.bio:
Dr. D. Shiva Prasad is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Secunderabad, Hyderabad, with more than 10 years of experience. His clinical interests include neuro-oncology, head and neck and thoracic cancers, prostate and bladder cancers, gynaecological malignancies and paediatric cancers.

His practice covers intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, external beam radiotherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. He also works with brachytherapy, including plaque brachytherapy, in which the radiation source is applied directly to the treatment site.

Dr. Prasad holds an MBBS and an MD in Radiation Oncology. His continuing education has been focused on the planning side of radiotherapy: in May 2018 he attended the ESTRO course on target volume determination from imaging to margins in Prague, which deals with how the treatment volume is defined from scans. He passed the European Society for Medical Oncology examination in September 2019.

In November 2017 he received a travel grant to attend the ESMO Preceptorship on Gastrointestinal Tumours in Singapore, where he presented a case on stereotactic body radiotherapy in locally recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma.

He is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and a member of the European Society for Radiotherapy & Oncology, the European Society for Medical Oncology and the American Society for Radiation Oncology.

dr-kushal-narang.bio:
Dr. Kushal Narang is Associate Director of Radiation Oncology and Cancer Care at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 20 years of experience. His clinical interests cover brain and spine tumors, head and neck cancers, lymphomas, pediatric cancers and genitourinary cancers of the prostate and bladder, and he also treats breast, lung and esophageal cancers along with malignancies of the stomach, liver, rectum and anal canal.

His technical expertise includes CyberKnife radiosurgery, stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, alongside intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. He performs both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

After completing his MBBS, Dr. Narang earned an MD in Radiation Oncology at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai. He later obtained a Professional Diploma in Clinical Research from Catalyst Clinical Services in New Delhi, which is reflected in his research role: he serves as principal investigator and co-investigator for multiple ongoing institutional and multi-institutional research projects.

In 2015 he gave an international paper presentation in Yokohama, Japan, on the use of CyberKnife SRS and SBRT for brain tumors and prostate cancers — the two areas where his stereotactic practice is most concentrated. In 2017 his work took third prize in the best paper session at the fifth National Conference of Young Radiation Oncologists of India, and since 2022 he has been Quality Champion of the Department of Radiation Oncology at Medanta in Gurugram.

dr-anita-malik.bio:
Dr. Anita Malik is Director of Radiation Oncology at Fortis Hospital, Noida, Delhi NCR, with more than 15 years of experience. Her practice covers the three main ways radiation is delivered in cancer treatment: from outside the body, from a focused stereotactic setup, and from a source placed within or close to the tumour.

On the external beam side she works with intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and conventional external beam radiotherapy. Her stereotactic expertise includes stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. She also performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy as well as intraoperative radiation therapy, which is given during an operation while the tumour bed is exposed.

Dr. Malik completed her MBBS at Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College in Jabalpur and her MD in Radiotherapy at Government Medical College, Indore. She subsequently attended an IMRT and IGRT clinical training course at National University Hospital in Singapore, adding focused preparation in image-guided and intensity-modulated delivery to her postgraduate radiotherapy education.

Alongside clinical work she writes for a general audience on cancer and radiation. Her published pieces cover the oral cancer signs every tobacco user should know, radiotherapy as an essential component of cancer treatment, and an explanation of how radiation therapy works — a useful indication of how she approaches explaining treatment to patients and families.

dr-susovan-banerjee.bio:
Dr. Susovan Banerjee is Director of Radiation Oncology at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 18 years of experience.

His clinical expertise includes intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy, along with stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy. He also performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Dr. Banerjee holds an MBBS and an MD, and completed a fellowship in image-guided gynaecological brachytherapy. That fellowship gives his practice a defined centre of gravity: brachytherapy for gynaecological cancers, where the radiation source is positioned within the body under imaging guidance, and where the interstitial technique he also uses becomes relevant for tumours that cannot be reached by intracavitary applicators alone. He consults at Medanta in Gurugram and at Medanta Mediclinic Defence Colony.

Alongside his clinical responsibilities he has contributed substantially to radiation oncology scholarship, with more than 53 full-text articles, invited editorials and multiple chapters in oncology textbooks to his name. He also serves as a section editor and reviewer for international radiotherapy journals, which keeps him close to the evidence as it is published.

He is a member of the Global Association of Physicians of Indian Origin and of the European Radiotherapy Society and the Indian association of radiation oncologists. As a departmental director, he combines specialist gynaecological brachytherapy, stereotactic and conformal treatment, and sustained academic engagement within one practice.

dr-natarajan-v.bio:
Dr. Natarajan V is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 11 years of experience. His clinical interests include brain tumors, head and neck cancers, breast cancer, gynecological malignancies and palliative radiation care.

His radiotherapy practice covers 3D conformal radiotherapy, image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy. He also works with stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery, and for cases suited to internal radiation he has experience in both intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Dr. Natarajan holds an MBBS and a DNB in Radiation Oncology. In February 2014 he trained in image-guided radiation therapy and real-time position management at Wirral in the United Kingdom. Real-time position management deals with the way a tumour moves as the patient breathes, so that preparation sits directly behind the image-guided and stereotactic work he does now, where accuracy of delivery is the point of the technique.

He is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and of the association's Tamil Nadu chapter. His academic activity includes a presentation titled "Year-End Review in Bone Tumors" at the Cancer Congress in Bangalore in 2017, and he has taken part in a number of cancer screening and awareness programmes.

dr-sandeep-goel.bio:
Dr. Sandeep Goel is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Artemis Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 15 years of experience. He treats brain tumours as well as cancers of the head and neck, thorax, breast, gastrointestinal tract and genitourinary system.

His radiation expertise includes 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. He also works with CyberKnife radiosurgery, conventional external beam radiotherapy, and intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy.

Dr. Goel earned his MBBS at Kasturba Medical College, Mangalore, and his MD in Radiation Oncology at Kasturba Medical College, Manipal. After postgraduate training he served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Radiotherapy and Oncology at Shirdi Sai Baba Cancer Hospital in Manipal before joining Artemis Hospitals in Gurugram, so his background combines teaching-hospital experience with private tertiary practice.

His interest in stereotactic treatment is backed by dedicated CyberKnife stereotactic radiotherapy training completed at Sunnyvale in the United States. That specialised preparation complements the conformal, image-guided and brachytherapy techniques he uses day to day.

His professional memberships include the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the association's Karnataka chapter and the Indian Brachytherapy Society, the last of these matching the intracavitary and interstitial work within his practice.

dr-anitha-gopinath.bio:
Dr. Anitha Gopinath is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 18 years of experience. She treats breast cancer, head and neck cancers, brain tumours, gynaecological cancers, lung cancers and gastrointestinal cancers.

Her areas of expertise include intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. She also works with external beam radiotherapy, CyberKnife radiosurgery, and intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, which allows the approach to be matched to the site and extent of disease.

Dr. Gopinath completed her MBBS and her MD in Radiation Oncology at Madras Medical College, and went on to a DNB in Radiation Oncology with post-doctorate training in the specialty in 2004 at the same institution. She subsequently worked at Apollo Specialty in Chennai before taking up her current appointment in Bangalore.

Her published work includes a rare case report, "1-Minute Bench to Lab and Lap to Lung", in the Journal of Neuro-Oncology, and a co-authored 2016 study on the challenges in treating carcinoma of the tongue in the Journal of Cancer Science and Therapy.

She is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the Indian Medical Association and the American Society for Radiation Oncology. In 2022 she was named Top Radiation Oncologist of South India by India Today and Best Radiation Oncologist of South India by Outlook Health.

dr-m-r-vishwateja.bio:
Dr. M. R. Vishwateja is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, Hyderabad, with more than 7 years of experience. He treats head and neck, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, gynaecological and thoracic cancers with radiation.

His technical scope includes image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, VMAT and MRI-guided radiotherapy, along with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. He also works with brachytherapy and total body irradiation, the latter used as part of conditioning before transplant, and has experience in external beam treatment and palliative care.

Dr. Vishwateja received his MBBS from Osmania Medical College, Hyderabad, in 2007 and completed his DNB in Radiation Oncology at Yashoda Cancer Institute, Hyderabad. He then undertook senior residency at MNJ Cancer Institute in Hyderabad. His wider clinical background includes St. Ann's Cancer Hospital in Kazipet, Warangal, and MGM Government Hospital in Warangal, giving him experience in both government and private cancer services.

In 2018 he completed training through the Indian College of Radiation Oncology, and in 2019 he obtained the Certification Course in Essentials of Palliative Care. That pairing of specialist radiotherapy training with palliative care education is reflected in his practice, which ranges from conventionally fractionated image-guided treatment given with curative intent to focused stereotactic approaches, brachytherapy, total body irradiation and radiation given primarily for symptom relief.

dr-k-kiran-kumar.bio:
Dr. K. Kiran Kumar is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, Hyderabad, with more than 19 years of experience in radiation oncology.

His practice covers radiation therapy for cancer, brachytherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and image-guided radiation therapy. He has a particular interest in RapidArc and in SRS and SRT, which extends his work across image-guided and highly focused forms of treatment. These methods differ mainly in how the dose is shaped and delivered: stereotactic techniques concentrate radiation on a defined target in a small number of sessions, while brachytherapy places the radiation source within or close to the area being treated.

Dr. Kumar completed an MD in Radiation Therapy followed by a DNB in the same discipline. That postgraduate training underpins his work across external radiation treatment, stereotactic techniques and brachytherapy at Yashoda Hospitals.

His disease-specific academic work centres on head and neck cancer, and he has served as principal investigator for multiple international clinical trials — a role that involves running studies to protocol at his own centre as part of a wider multi-country programme.

He maintains professional connections with the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, the Indian Medical Association and the European Society for Medical Oncology, keeping his practice linked to both Indian and international oncology communities.

dr-neha-sehgal.bio:
Dr. Neha Sehgal is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Fortis Hospital, Noida, Delhi NCR, with more than 10 years of experience.

Her technical expertise includes 3D conformal radiotherapy, external beam radiotherapy, image-guided radiation therapy and intensity-modulated radiation therapy. These are the techniques behind most courses of curative radiation: the dose is shaped to the tumour and checked against imaging before delivery.

She also works with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, where a high dose is concentrated on a small, well-defined target over a few sessions, and with intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, where the radiation source is placed within or beside the area being treated. Her range further includes CyberKnife and Gamma Knife radiosurgery, intraoperative radiation therapy given during an operation, and proton beam therapy.

Taken together, that span covers conventionally fractionated external beam treatment, highly focused stereotactic delivery, radiation administered in theatre and radiation delivered from inside the body, which is what allows the technique to be chosen on clinical grounds for each plan.

Dr. Sehgal holds an MBBS and an MD, and completed an international observer experience at Froedtert Hospital and the Medical College of Wisconsin in the United States.
